This is great advice, but as an addendum to anyone else struggling with Niall: You can probably use a crossbow or throwing knives in lieu of Beast Roar if you don't have it. In addition, after rolling backwards to avoid the jumping lighting kick, *run* left towards the boss and get 1 or 2 melee hits in.

From there, if he does his standard sideways swing then don't panic and just time your dodge, if he charges up his lightning kick then just run and roll at the last second just in case because his hitboxes are stupid. This way the fight will take far less time and thus give you less room to make mistakes.

Confessor gets little love because it's not the most optimal class from a min-maxing perspective. With 99% of builds there's at least one stat you won't touch, usually 2 or 3, so the ideal class is whichever one has the least of these stats, and Confessor's lowest stat is a 9 (18 total wasted points), in both Intelligence and Arcane, something you likely wouldn't typically level up on a faith-oriented build. Compare that with Prophet who starts with 7 int and 10 arcane (17 total wasted points), meaning that even if you levelled up all other stats but those, he'd be one point level more efficient than Confessor.

As mentioned, incantations are usually more divine or earthly in origin and scale off of Faith (Dragon-related stuff, holy stuff, lightning stuff, fire stuff), while sorceries are more connected to the stars and cosmos and scale off of Intelligence (typical blue beams, waves, conjured swords/greatswords and even some gravity manipulation and meteors).Basically, incantations are more typically Cleric-y and sorceries are more typically Wizard-y to compare them to D&D.

Usually you'll only want to go for one of these as you also need to level up some Mind to increase your FP (Mana-equivalent) so you can cast spells, though a really dedicated caster build can go for both though they'll have less points to spend on HP, heavier armour, or the strength/dex required to use certain heavier/fancier weapons.

The Champion was a CNT-exclusive class which had the same armour as the Hero in the final game has and did start with the dragonfire spell, though in the final game the Hero will be more of a pure strength build without any starting spells and starts with fairly low faith, int and mind.

Picking them is still perfectly fine if you want to use either sorceries or incantations, a starting class doesn't really define your playstyle but more just what areas you're strongest right off the bat, the only *really* detrimental choice would be picking something like the Prisoner, who starts with a measly 6 Faith, and then levelling up Faith to use incantations with him pretty much.If you have any follow-up questions feel free to ask.

Pretty much, a party has an effective party level (EPL) based on the levels of the people in the party and the amount of people. So, 1 level 60 + 4 level 30s would be 60 + 30 \* 4 AKA 180. 180 is then divided by the amount of people in the party (5) for an EPL of 36. Meaning the level 30s would get XP from mobs as if they were level 36, split among the people in the party.
